For the preparation-stage reading sequence, use [solver observations](course/solver-observations.qmd). This page owns the stored-mesh diagnostic contract.

`scgsim.palace.check_mesh_quality()` reads a solver-bound Gmsh MSH 2.2 ASCII
file without starting Gmsh or Palace. It returns an immutable
`MeshQualityReport` for the linear four-node tetrahedra that are actually in
that file. This is a diagnostic reading surface, not a mesh repair step and not
a scientific acceptance gate.

Palace meshes can store curved high-order elements. This reader computes quality
metrics only for native Gmsh type-4 four-node tetrahedra.
Higher-order elements are counted separately and excluded from these metrics,
so a mesh containing only higher-order tetrahedra has no 3D quality metric.
Use the Palace
[mesh summary](specs/palace-electrostatic-sgb.qmd#mesh-manifest-and-detached-summary)
for recorded geometric order, native element types, and generation statistics.

This reader is separate from the quality audit that `mesh()` runs. That audit
measures the minimum signed inverse condition number (minSICN) on the linear mesh before any
elevation to the geometry order, holds it to the mesh's quality threshold and
writes its own report; see the
[Palace mesh controls](specs/palace-electrostatic-sgb.qmd#palace-mesh-controls).
The sizes the audited mesh starts from, including those at film walls and on
Surface-EPR band boundary curves, are the sizing recipe's
([Sizing recipes](specs/palace-electrostatic-sgb.qmd#palace-mesh-recipes)).
`check_mesh_quality()` measures the stored solver mesh after elevation, with
different metrics, and applies no threshold. The two reports do not replace each
other.

Generation edge statistics are separate from `MeshQualityReport`. The Palace
summary records each physical region's unique primary-corner edge count and
minimum, mean, and maximum straight chord lengths in micrometres. These remain
chords on curved high-order elements; they are not curved arc lengths or a
higher-order quality metric. Point regions have zero edges and no length
extrema. Missing historical statistics remain `not_recorded` rather than
being inferred by this tetrahedron reader.

## Version identities of a mesh {#version-identities}

A mesh that `mesh()` writes carries three versions. Read them to tell whether
two meshes were made the same way.

::: {.askr-table-compact}
| Identity | Example | Where it is recorded | When it changes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Package version | `scgsim 2.0.0rc15` | `scgsim_version` in the run's provenance (`metadata/route_b_provenance.json`, or `route_a_…` on Route A) | With every release of SCGSim. |
| Recipe version | `scgsim.meshing.features/N` for `FeatureRecipe`, `scgsim.meshing.uniform-boundary/N` for `UniformBoundaryRecipe`, `scgsim.meshing.global-size/N` for `GlobalSizeRecipe` | `recipe.version` in each quality report and in the mesh manifest, beside `recipe.parameters` | Only when the sizes the recipe asks for change. |
| Report format | `scgsim.meshing.report/N` | `report_version` in each quality report | When the fields of the quality report change. |
:::

A recipe's version goes up only when the sizes it asks for change. `FeatureRecipe`
went from `features/1` to `features/2` when it began to size every Surface-EPR
band boundary curve. So two reports with the same recipe version and the same
parameters asked for the same initial sizes, even when they were made by
different package releases; a different recipe version means the meshes were
made by different sizing rules. The recipe version covers the initial sizes
only: the repair policy is recorded in each report, and the Gmsh version in the
mesh manifest.

The versions are separate because one version for the whole meshing module
would change whenever any recipe changed, and could not say which one did. A
run with `UniformBoundaryRecipe` keeps its version when `FeatureRecipe` changes,
so its reports stay comparable across that change.

For example, the same default `FeatureRecipe()` on a flip-chip qubit with bands
of 0.5 and 1 µm (the OrcaPen SC PDK `disk_flip_chip_qubit` under common ground
planes, Route B) gives two different meshes under the two versions:

::: {.askr-table-compact}
| | `scgsim.meshing.features/1` | `scgsim.meshing.features/2` |
|---|---|---|
| Sizes asked for | 1.30 µm on the 801 film-wall curves | 1.30 µm on 3,104 curves: the film walls and every band boundary curve |
| First mesh | 402,784 tetrahedra, 1 below the quality threshold | 569,325 tetrahedra, none below it |
| Result | clean after one repair round: 407,093 tetrahedra, 82.5 s | clean in the first mesh: 569,325 tetrahedra, 53.4 s |
:::

The two quality reports name different recipe versions, so the different mesh
comes from the sizing rules, not from anything else in the run.

## Input and ownership

The reader accepts only MSH 2.2 ASCII files and preserves node and element IDs,
element order, original binary64 coordinates, raw tag order, and
dimension-qualified physical names. Other element types are counted but are
not silently reinterpreted as linear tetrahedra. Known public MSH element codes
must have their standard node arity; future unknown codes remain counted as
unknown rather than acquiring a guessed dimension. Missing node references and
nonfinite coordinates stay attached to their element IDs as unavailable
records; malformed sections and duplicate IDs fail closed.

Reading is sequential. The report binds the parsed byte count, SHA-256, and
before/after file identity, and does not retain an open file or reread the mesh
for later summaries, export, or visualization. A report owns read-only compact
arrays. Returned dictionaries and Plotly figures are detached presentation
objects and cannot mutate retained measurements.

## Numerical meaning

For authored tetrahedron vertices \(p_0,p_1,p_2,p_3\), the edge matrix is

\[
B = [p_1-p_0\; p_2-p_0\; p_3-p_0].
\]

The signed mesh-unit volume is \(\det(B)/6\); the reported volume magnitude is
\(|\det(B)|/6\). Orientation and magnitude are separate: a positive,
negative, or exact-zero orientation is never inferred from a rounded absolute
volume.

The fast orientation path first applies one exactly reversible power-of-two
scale to all twelve coordinates of the element, before subtraction. It uses a
Shewchuk-style determinant error bound \(E=(7+56u)uP\), with binary64 unit
roundoff \(u=2^{-53}\) and \(P\) formed in the matching triple-product order,
only for the sign decision. A bound
that is inconclusive, a scale that loses a finite nonzero value, or a
representation-boundary ambiguity takes the exact fallback based on
`float.as_integer_ratio()` values from the original coordinates. Nonfinite
coordinates remain locatable but numerically unavailable. The report
retains the determinant estimate, absolute sign bound, and the selected
method. The exact fallback computes mesh-unit and optional SI volume
independently before either result is rounded to binary64, so mesh and SI
underflow or overflow remain distinct statuses rather than false zero or
infinity.

The condition metric uses

\[
J = B W^{-1},\qquad
W = \begin{bmatrix}
1 & 1/2 & 1/2 \\
0 & \sqrt{3}/2 & \sqrt{3}/6 \\
0 & 0 & \sqrt{2/3}
\end{bmatrix},
\qquad \kappa(J)=\sigma_{max}/\sigma_{min}.
\]

A regular reference tetrahedron therefore has \(\kappa=1\). Exact zero
determinants are singular. A nonzero exact determinant whose smallest singular
value is below the numerical-resolution threshold is reported as numerically
unresolved, not relabeled geometrically singular.
The threshold is \(\sigma_{min}\leq3\epsilon\sigma_{max}\), with binary64
spacing \(\epsilon=2^{-52}\). It is a reporting status, not a scientific
quality gate.

## Units, summaries, and ranking

`length_scale_m` is optional. Without it, mesh-unit volume is available and SI
volume is explicitly unavailable. Palace simulation wrappers pass their
existing micrometre model scale (`1e-6`) after a mesh has been built. A direct
call may supply another finite positive scale but does not infer one from the
file.

Summaries keep available values, exact singularities, numerical-resolution
failures, missing nodes, nonfinite coordinates, and representation failures in
separate counts. Volume and condition statistics state their units, sample
count, and excluded count; a metric with no comparable samples says so
explicitly. The median, 95th percentile, and 99th percentile use the binary64
position \((n-1)q\) with rational interpolation between the two selected
binary64 endpoints. Statistics and worst-element ranks use only values whose
status makes them comparable.

Condition-number ranking places exact singularities first, then finite values
in descending order; volume ranking is ascending. Element ID breaks ties
deterministically. Each display has a ranked group and a separately visible
unavailable/remainder group. `limit=10` can therefore show up to ten rows from
each group, while `limit=0` shows none. An element that lacks the *other*
metric remains eligible when its selected metric is comparable. These ranks
describe the selected diagnostic metric only and do not impose a pass/fail
threshold.

`show_summary()` and `show_worst_elements()` provide text displays.
`show_elements()` imports Plotly lazily and draws the six authored edges for
each selected tetrahedron as lines and its four vertices once as markers, with
`aspectmode="data"`. Degenerate vertices remain visible without rewriting
coordinates or inflating a tiny nonzero dimension. The figure title reports
selected and drawn counts for each group, and undrawable IDs and reasons are
visible annotations. Explicit `element_ids` preserve caller order, ignore the
ranking limit, accept Python and NumPy integers other than booleans, and reject
other types. Unknown requested element IDs fail instead of being dropped.

These inert coordinate sets illustrate three distinct outcomes; they are not
executed by the documentation build and do not define acceptance thresholds:

```python
# p0, p1, p2, p3 in authored mesh units
regular = ((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), (0.5, 3**0.5 / 2, 0),
           (0.5, 3**0.5 / 6, (2 / 3)**0.5))
coplanar = ((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), (0, 1, 0), (1, 1, 0))
thin_nonzero = ((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), (0, 1, 0), (0, 0, 2**-100))
```

The regular set uses the documented reference matrix and has
\(\kappa(J)=1\). The coplanar set is exactly singular. With the shown
`2**-100` height, the thin set has a nonzero orientation and volume but a
numerically unresolved condition number; the report keeps those facts
separate.

## Serialization and limitations

`to_dict()` returns detached plain containers. `save_json()` validates and
strictly serializes the complete header before exclusively creating the output,
then streams nodes and elements without materializing the complete report. It
refuses to overwrite either an existing path or the mesh itself. Nonfinite or
unavailable numerical values are serialized as `null` with an explicit reason.
Exact-singular condition number is the distinct JSON string `"+inf"`; JSON
never contains bare `NaN` or `Infinity` tokens. A later operating-system write
failure can leave a partial newly created output file; this is streaming output,
not an atomic replacement protocol.

Text summaries use `+inf` for an exact-singular condition number. Strict JSON
cannot encode infinity as a number, so the corresponding value is the string
`"+inf"`; its status retains the distinction from missing or unresolved data.

For an actual Palace mesh, the [solver-observation lesson](course/solver-observations.qmd) shows the source-bound summary and figures. Direct callers may use `check_mesh_quality(mesh_path, length_scale_m=...)` and the same report methods.


The two-group limit applies independently to comparable ranked elements and
the visible unavailable/remainder group, so `limit=10` can display as many as
twenty rows or elements. `save_json()` refuses an existing destination; choose
a new path for each diagnostic capture.

This V1 surface does not reorder tetrahedra to match solver orientation, repair
connectivity, evaluate higher-order tetrahedra, infer solver-side acceptance,
or prove convergence. It reads the stored mesh exactly once and reports its
own numerical evidence.

The numerical design follows Shewchuk's
[adaptive-predicate guidance](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~quake/robust.html) for
sign decisions and uses NumPy's documented
[SVD rank-resolution model](https://numpy.org/doc/stable/reference/generated/numpy.linalg.matrix_rank.html)
only as a numerical-resolution indicator. The
[MFEM mesh implementation](https://docs.mfem.org/4.9/mesh_8cpp_source.html) may
reorder elements in its own workflow; that does not redefine the orientation
of the original MSH connectivity inspected here.
